footnote: Day and week labels mark routine stages, not study timings. AI illustrations, not real results.
image_prompt: Empty background scene only: a pure white seamless paper backdrop, soft daylight from the upper left, a faint grey contact-shadow area on the right. Square 1080x1080. Keep the right 45% of the frame as an empty space, evenly lit, for a pack photo placed later, and keep the left half as a calm empty area for copy. No product, no bottle, no packaging, no text, no letters, no logos, no people, no faces, no skin, no hands.
headline: 5% Marula Oil in a daily routine
caption: Marula Oil 5% Face Moisturizer: 5% is the Marula Oil strength stated on the page; use AM & PM. The frames are AI illustrations of a routine, not study results.
photography_needed: Real, consented progress photos from a documented study of this product (same person, same light; the real pack in frame) to replace the AI frames before any use.
layout_description: Headline top; three progress frames of the same AI-illustrated skin area left to right (Day 1, Week 2, Week 4), the real pack placed small in the lower-right of EVERY frame; AI-GENERATED mark; footnote states that the labels are routine stages and the frames are illustrations.
frames_prompt: Three equal panels of the same Indian woman in her early 40s with medium-brown skin, an identical close crop of the cheek in every panel, same framing, angle and soft daylight from the upper left. Concern: dry skin. Panel 1: a few faint dry, dull patches; panel 2: slightly smoother; panel 3: slightly smoother again. The change is small and realistic, never dramatic; natural pores and texture in all three. In every panel the lower-right corner (about 30% of the panel width and 40% of its height) is a plain, softly lit area that is intentionally empty, reserved for the real pack to be placed later.
adaptation_notes: Format #14 Progress / timeline REMAKE (PAIRS 'remake'): subtle, with the product visible in every frame (the AI image leaves a plain empty corner in each panel and the REAL pack cut-out is composited there by code, pack_in_frames; the image model never draws the product). The concern (dry skin, F9) is shown with a small, realistic change only, never dramatic. Labels are routine stages with no result wording and the footnote says so (no study timing is claimed); the headline names the active and strength only. Reuses the dry-skin frames already generated for the Vitamin B5 moisturizer ad. Severe, AI-labelled, not exportable until real study photos replace the frames.
